```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
has_scip <- requireNamespace("scip", quietly = TRUE)
has_osqp <- requireNamespace("osqp", quietly = TRUE)
has_nloptr <- requireNamespace("nloptr", quietly = TRUE)
```

```{r setup}
library(optcompR)
```

optcompR describes an optimization problem once, as variables, expressions,
constraints and an objective, and then classifies it, chooses a capable solver
Every backend is registered with the problem classes it accepts, the classes
it solves to global optimality and the features it supports.

```{r}
opt_solvers()
opt_solver_capabilities("highs")
```

## Support matrix

| Backend | Classes | Global for | Duals | Ranging | Warm start |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| highs | LP, MILP, convex QP | all of these | LP, QP | LP | yes |
| scip | LP, MILP, QP, MIQP, QCQP, MIQCQP | all, including nonconvex | no | no | no |
| osqp | convex QP, LP | convex problems | yes | no | no |
| nloptr | NLP, QCQP, QP, LP (SLSQP) | convex problems | estimated by `opt_check()` | no | start point |
| roi | whatever the chosen ROI plugin solves | plugin | plugin | no | no |

Not supported in this version: conic programs (SOCP, SDP), general MINLP,
indicator and SOS constraints, IPOPT.

## Automatic choice

`solver = "auto"` picks the highest priority backend that accepts the class
and convexity of the model. For nonconvex problems global solvers come first.
When nothing fits, the error explains why each backend was rejected:

```{r, error = TRUE}
m <- opt_model()
x <- opt_variable(m, "x", type = "integer", lower = 0, upper = 3)
opt_objective(m, exp(x))
opt_solve(m)
```

## Comparing backends on one model

```{r}
m <- opt_model()
x <- opt_variable(m, "x", dim = 3, lower = 0)
opt_constraint(m, sum(x) >= 1)
opt_objective(m, sum((x - c(0.2, 0.5, 0.1))^2) + x[1] * x[2])
solvers <- intersect(c("highs", "osqp", "scip", "nloptr"), with(opt_solvers(), solver[available]))
res <- lapply(solvers, function(s) opt_solve(m, solver = s))
data.frame(solver = solvers,
           status = vapply(res, opt_status, ""),
           objective = vapply(res, opt_objective_value, 0),
           max_row_violation = vapply(res, function(r) opt_check(r)$max_row_violation, 0))
```

The objective in every result is evaluated from the model, not copied from
the solver, so the numbers are comparable. `opt_objective_value(r, solver =
TRUE)` returns the solver's own value.

## ROI plugins

```{r, eval = requireNamespace("ROI.plugin.glpk", quietly = TRUE)}
m <- opt_model("max")
x <- opt_variable(m, "x", dim = 2, type = "integer", lower = 0)
opt_constraint(m, 2 * x[1] + 3 * x[2] <= 12)
opt_objective(m, 3 * x[1] + 4 * x[2])
r <- opt_solve(m, solver = "roi", options = list(roi_solver = "glpk"))
opt_value(r, x)
```

## Solver options

Options are passed through to the backend; for HiGHS they override defaults:

```{r}
r <- opt_solve(m, solver = "highs", options = list(presolve = "off"))
opt_status(r)
```
